LM Studio has added Z.ai's new GLM-5.3-Flash model to its Bionic AI agent platform, supporting multimodal input, a 1 million token context window, and pricing significantly lower than GLM-5.2. Details below.

LM Studio acts fast to bring GLM-5.3-Flash to Bionic

Since its initial launch in mid-July, LM Studio has been continuously expanding the models and features available on the Bionic platform. Bionic is a Mac and Windows platform for agentic tasks such as coding, research, and handling documents and files.

LM Studio Bionic can use locally run models, as well as cloud models hosted on servers within the United States, the latter protected by a strict zero data retention policy.

Shortly after launching LM Studio Bionic, the company added support for Moonshot AI Kimi K3. Today, the company announces cloud support for Z.ai's new GLM-5.3-Flash model. LM Studio says running GLM-5.3-Flash costs up to 10 times less than GLM-5.2.

LM Studio's announcement came just hours after Z.ai officially released GLM-5.3-Flash. This model had already attracted considerable attention while being anonymously tested on OpenCode and OpenRouter under the codename "Ox Alpha".

GLM-5.3-Flash is a 320 billion parameter mixture-of-experts model that activates 18 billion parameters at a time, supports image and text input, and features a 1 million token context window.

In the benchmark tests highlighted by Z.ai, GLM-5.3-Flash scores ahead of GLM-5.2, with overall performance at a comparable level to frontier models from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and DeepSeek.
